newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end at 70-mth high, eye record.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end at 70-mth high, eye record.

text.p: Austria's ATX index raced ahead more than one percent on Wednesday to finish at a fresh 70-month high and market participants said the record close of April 1991 was coming within reach.
The 21-share ATX closed 12.34 points, or 1.01 percent, higher at 1,235.79 in brisk trade -- within sight of its lifetime high of 1,257.96.
"Today's performance has confirmed yesterday's technical break-out. The sky's the limit," a trader said.

Creditanstalt preferred shares carried the market, surging 19.5 schillings, or 4.33 percent, to 469.5 schillings on 166,830 lots. Creditanstalt ordinaries were the second most actively traded stock. They were 12 schillings up at 710 on 132,273 lots.

Investors have returned in force to Creditanstalt shares in recent days, apparently confident that the bank's takeover by rival Bank Austria will work in their favour. Creditanstalt shares took a battering immediately after the sale was announced in January.
Oil and chemicals group OMV, Vienna airport company Flughafen Wien and engineering group VA Tech also found favour with investors. OMV and Flughafen touched new year highs.
Overall 15 ATX shares closed higher, three lower and three unchanged. March ATX futures stood 17.0 points up at 1,245.0.
The leading decliner was fibre maker Lenzing, which slumped 21 schillings, or 3.48 pct, to 583 schillings.
The Vienna bourse index was up 3.64 points at 456.28.
